passage:
The oldest lunch table in the cafeteria had many scratches. The school planned to replace it.
Before it was removed, students noticed names and small drawings on its surface. Some were from years ago. A teacher even found her own name from when she had been a student.
The school decided to cut a small piece from the table and display it near the cafeteria entrance.
The new tables were cleaner and safer, but the old piece reminded everyone of students who had eaten, talked, worried, and laughed there before.
A table is usually just furniture. But after many years, it can become a record of ordinary days.
